decisions.reason: For integral mu, W_mu=W; the single-wall dot stabilizer is S_mu={1,s_alpha}. In rank one W={1,s_alpha}, so the original assertion that these subgroups are distinct is false. The datum and translating weight remain valid; repaired the clarification to state equality in rank one and inequality in higher rank.

The cited abelian/extension theorem requires an h-semisimple middle term; its sl2 induced Borel Jordan extension shows this cannot be dropped. F3 omitted that qualification. This unused assertion is nonfatal: steps 1.1 and 2.1 only use a projective onto each simple, an indecomposable cover summand, finite composition series, and subquotients already in O. Corrected F3 and removed its unnecessary length-additivity assertion; the Statement and proof remain unchanged.

Neither the composition-series definition nor the finite-length theorem establishes series independence, so original F3 had an essential dependency-citation gap. Added the existing Jordan–Hölder theorem, and proved short-exact-sequence additivity by concatenating a series of the subobject with inverse images of a quotient series. Also justified scalar endomorphisms using the cyclic one-dimensional highest line and stated where finiteness of Hom dimensions follows in the induction.

The long exact Ext supplier assumes an abelian category with enough projectives and injectives and supplied resolutions on all objects. Original F3 quoted its conclusion without discharging these interface hypotheses. The needed mathematics exists in the supplier closure, including the orthogonality lemma F3, but the application lacked explicit prerequisite evidence. Added the enough-projectives and exact-duality suppliers, proved enough injectives by dualizing projective epimorphisms, and supplied AC-chosen resolutions on a set-sized skeleton; AC also implies DC.

The decomposition lemma assumes every object of its abelian category has finite length; it does not prove this for O. Original F3 attributed both finite length and decomposition to that conditional supplier. Added the published finite-length and abelian-category theorems to F3 and deps, so all hypotheses are verified before step 1.2. Exact duality reverses a projective Verma flag into a costandard flag, and BGG reciprocity gives the stated multiplicities.

reviews.reason: Corrected the false subgroup inequality: S_mu=W_mu=W in rank one and S_mu is proper in higher rank. Real wall-sign conventions, the codimension-one datum, integral translating weight, and its dominant representative remain valid. Examined all four direct item consumers and the owning page; none uses the removed inequality.

Qualified extension closure by h-semisimplicity and removed unused length-additivity prose. The projective onto each simple splits off a cover in its linkage class. Along a finite composition series, lifting each top simple cover and adding the preceding epimorphism gives a surjection from a finite sum of covers. Zero uses the empty sum. Statement unchanged.

Jordan–Hölder now supplies series independence; concatenation proves additivity. Every map from the cover to a simple factors through its unique head; the cyclic highest line gives End(L)=C. Exact projective Hom and induction give finite-dimensional Hom and the composition-factor count. Statement unchanged; no new prerequisite item.

Explicitly verified the long-exact theorem hypotheses: O is abelian with enough projectives and injectives, AC supplies resolutions on a set-sized skeleton, and AC implies DC. At each flag step the fourth and sixth Ext terms vanish, so the middle Ext term vanishes and Hom dimensions add. This proves both formulas for all labels. Statement unchanged.

The finite-length and abelian-category theorems now discharge the decomposition lemma hypotheses. Exact duality reverses each Verma flag into a costandard flag; BGG gives its multiplicities. Each indecomposable injective dualizes to a projective cover of its simple head. Concatenating the finite summand flags includes zero. Statement unchanged.
